title: Binary syndrome decoding

problem.name: Binary syndrome decoding
problem.statement_latex: Given a full-rank binary parity-check matrix $H\in\mathbb F_2^{(n-k)\times n}$, a syndrome $s$, and weight $w$, find $e\in\mathbb F_2^n$ with $He=s$ and $|e|=w$. Random instances model generic attacks on code-based cryptography. Complexity is measured in quantum gate time and classical bit-operation time, with coherent list-access costs specified for quantum walks.
problem.statement_text: Given a full-rank binary parity-check matrix $H\in\mathbb F_2^{(n-k)\times n}$, a syndrome $s$, and weight $w$, find $e\in\mathbb F_2^n$ with $He=s$ and $|e|=w$. Random instances model generic attacks on code-based cryptography. Complexity is measured in quantum gate time and classical bit-operation time, with coherent list-access costs specified for quantum walks.

quantum.headline_latex: $\operatorname{poly}(n)\sqrt{\binom nw/\binom{n-k}{w}}$, amplified Prange; parameter-dependent improvements from quantum-walk ISD.
quantum.headline_text: $\operatorname{poly}(n)\sqrt{\binom nw/\binom{n-k}{w}}$, amplified Prange; parameter-dependent improvements from quantum-walk ISD.
quantum.details_latex: For $w\le n-k$, $p=\binom{n-k}{w}/\binom nw$ is the success probability of one Prange information-set trial in the usual random-code model. Reversible elimination, the weight test and uncomputation enter its polynomial cost. Kachigar--Tillich and Kirshanova accelerate internal list matching as well as the outer search. The $0.05869$ exponent is the maximum over rates at Gilbert--Varshamov weight in the Kachigar--Tillich comparison; concrete attacks optimize the actual $n,k,w$.

classical.headline_latex: The minimum of optimized BJMM/May--Ozerov ISD and applicable sparse-circuit counting; Prange costs $\operatorname{poly}(n)/p$.
classical.headline_text: The minimum of optimized BJMM/May–Ozerov ISD and applicable sparse-circuit counting; Prange costs $\operatorname{poly}(n)/p$.
classical.details_latex: For dense random constant-rate codes, the classical comparator minimizes the parameter-dependent representation and nearest-neighbor costs of modern ISD. If $H$ has $h$ nonzero entries, the predicate $He=s$, $|e|=w$ has an $O(n+h)$-gate Boolean circuit. Tensor contraction and witness recovery give deterministic time $\operatorname{poly}(n+h)2^{O((n+h)/\sqrt{\log(n+h)})}$. For $h=O(n)$ this is $2^{O(n/\sqrt{\log n})}$. Dense matrices have $h=\Theta(n^2)$, where optimized ISD supplies the stronger displayed bound.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial speedup for dense random codes: quadratic acceleration of Prange and further reductions in the exponential constant from quantum walks. Sparse parity checks have the stated subexponential classical comparator.

evidence.description_latex: Partial evidence for a total-runtime separation on explicit dense codes; amplification rigorously improves a specified trial success probability.

hardware.description_latex:
Reversible elimination uses polynomial logical space. Advanced walks trade runtime for exponentially large coherent list storage. Cryptographic instances require fault-tolerant arithmetic and many coherent trial evaluations.

{\small [Before ``ETH is false'', the classical sparse-code comparison used exponential-time ISD, and quantum amplification reduced a Prange trial cost from $\operatorname{poly}(n)/p$ to $\operatorname{poly}(n)/\sqrt p$.]\par}
